## Overview

Apps are the actual applications managed by datamitsu. Unlike [Tools](tools.md) which are configurations, Apps are the binaries and packages that get installed and executed.

This configuration manages **118 apps** across multiple runtimes (binary, bun, node, python, go, jvm).

## Apps by Category

- **Code Generation** (6 apps): buf, openapi-generator, protoc, etc.
- **Containers & Kubernetes** (5 apps): crane, dive, gcrane, etc.
- **Database Migrations** (2 apps): golang-migrate, goose
- **Data Processing** (4 apps): dasel, fx, jq, etc.
- **Documentation & Spelling** (10 apps): cspell, d2, harper-cli, etc.
- **Git & Releases** (8 apps): commitlint, conventional-changelog, dm-internal-lefthook-upstream, etc.
- **HTTP & gRPC Clients** (3 apps): grpcurl, httpstat, xh
- **Infrastructure as Code** (4 apps): terraform-docs, terragrunt, tfupdate, etc.
- **Linters & Formatters** (42 apps): actionlint, alint, ast-grep, etc.
- **Package Managers** (2 apps): pnpm, utpm
- **Secrets & Signing** (4 apps): age, age-keygen, cosign, etc.
- **Security Scanners** (20 apps): bandit, bearer, blint, etc.
- **Task Runners & Dev Servers** (3 apps): air, just, task
- **Type Checkers** (3 apps): mypy, tsc, ty
- **Utilities** (2 apps): allurectl, oxipng

## How Apps Work

When you run `dm init`, datamitsu:

1. Downloads and caches app binaries based on your project types
2. Supports multiple runtimes:
   - **binary** — Native executables (Go, Rust compiled tools)
   - **bun** — npm packages and bundled scripts executed via managed Bun
   - **node** — npm packages executed via Node.js
   - **python** — Python packages installed via pip/uv
3. Apps are referenced by [Tools](tools.md) configurations

When you run `dm check`, datamitsu executes [Tools](tools.md), which invoke Apps with configured arguments and file globs.
